The Hades sequence was filmed on the black sand beaches of Hjörleifshöfði, Iceland, where the midnight sun means daylight never completely disappears. Nolan deliberately chose the location because its cold, almost otherworldly landscape couldn’t feel further removed from the Mediterranean world of Odysseus. It was his third time shooting in Iceland, following Batman Begins (2005) and Interstellar (2014). For this particular scene Nolan used no CGI no green screens, instead he buried his actors in black sand and mud to bring the Greek underworld to life.

The Odyssey (2026) already made cinema history as the first feature film shot entirely on IMAX film cameras. After grossing a staggering $1.8 billion worldwide, including $550 million from IMAX screenings alone, the film is returning to more than 1,000 theaters on December 11, including IMAX and IMAX 70mm, for its awards-season run.

An absolute masterpiece, but do YOU think The Odyssey lived up to the hype?
